1.1: Since many have indeed taken in hand to put in order an account of the matters completely confirmed among us,
1.2: as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the Word delivered them to us,
1.3: it seemed good to me as well, having followed up all these matters exactly from the beginning, to write to you an orderly account, most excellent Theophilos,
1.4: that you might know the certainty of the Words which you were taught.
1.5: There was in the days of Hĕrodĕs, the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, a certain kohĕn named Zeḵaryah, of the division of Aḇiyah. And his wife was of the daughters of Aharon, and her name was Elisheḇa.
1.6: And they were both righteous before Elohim, blamelessly walking in all the Commands and Righteousnesses of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.7: And they had no child, because Elisheḇa was barren, and both were advanced in years.
1.8: And it came to be, that while he was serving as kohĕn before Elohim in the order of his division,
1.9: according to the institute of the kehunnah, he was chosen by lot to burn incense when he went into the Mishkan of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.10: And the entire crowd of people was praying outside at the hour of incense.
1.11: And a messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared to him, standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
1.12: And when Zeḵaryah saw, he was troubled, and fear fell upon him.
1.13: But the messenger said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zeḵaryah, for your prayer is heard. And your wife Elisheḇa shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Yoḥanan.
1.14: “And you shall have joy and gladness, and many shall rejoice at his birth.
1.15: “For he shall be great before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and shall drink no wine and strong drink at all. And he shall be filled with the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, even from his mother’s womb.
1.16: “And he shall turn many of the children of Yisra’ĕl to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim.
1.17: “And he shall go before Him in the spirit and power of Ĕliyahu, ‘to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children,’ and the disobedient to the insight of the righteous, to make ready a people prepared for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
1.18: And Zeḵaryah said to the messenger, “By what shall I know this? For I am old, and my wife advanced in years.”
1.19: And the messenger answering, said to him, “I am Gaḇri’ĕl, who stands in the presence of Elohim, and was sent to speak to you and announce to you this good news.
1.20: “But see, you shall be silent and unable to speak until the day this takes place, because you did not believe my words which shall be filled in their appointed time.”
1.21: And the people waited for Zeḵaryah, and marveled at his delay in the Mishkan.
1.22: And when he came out, he was unable to speak to them. And they recognized that he had seen a vision in the Mishkan, for he was beckoning to them and remained dumb.
1.23: And it came to be, as soon as the days of his service were completed, he went away to his house.
1.24: And after those days his wife Elisheḇa conceived. And she hid herself five months, saying,
1.25: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has done this for me, in the days when He looked upon me, to take away my reproach among men.”
1.26: And in the sixth month the messenger Gaḇri’ĕl was sent by Elohim to a city of Galil named Natsareth,
1.27: to a maiden engaged to a man whose name was Yosĕph, of the house of Dawiḏ. And the maiden’s name was Miryam.
1.28: And the messenger, coming to her, said, “Greetings, favored one, the Aḏon is with you.”
1.29: But she was greatly disturbed at his word, and wondered what kind of greeting this was.
1.30: And the messenger said to her, “Do not be afraid, Miryam, for you have found favor with Elohim.
1.31: “And see, you shall conceive in your womb, and shall give birth to a Bĕn, and call His Name 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
1.32: “He shall be great, and shall be called the Bĕn of the Most High. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim shall give Him the throne of His father Dawiḏ.
1.33: “And He shall reign over the house of Ya’aqoḇ forever, and there shall be no end to His Malḵuth.”
1.34: And Miryam said to the messenger, “How shall this be, since I do not know a man?”
1.35: And the messenger answering, said to her, “The Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh shall come upon you, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow you. And for that reason the Qadosh One born of you shall be called: Bĕn of Elohim.
1.36: “And see, Elisheḇa your relative, she has also conceived a son in her old age. And this is now the sixth month to her who was called barren,
1.37: because with Elohim no matter shall be impossible.”
1.38: And Miryam said, “See the female servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄! Let it be to me according to your word.” And the messenger went away from her.
1.39: And Miryam arose in those days and went into the hill country with haste, to a city of Yahuḏah,
1.40: and entered into the house of Zeḵaryah and greeted Elisheḇa.
1.41: And it came to be, when Elisheḇa heard the greeting of Miryam, that the infant leaped in her womb. And Elisheḇa was filled with the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh,
1.42: and called out with a loud voice and said, “Beruḵah are you among women, and baruḵ is the fruit of your womb!
1.43: “And who am I, that the mother of Aḏonai should come to me?
1.44: “For look, when the sound of your greeting came to my ears, the infant in my womb leaped for joy.
1.45: “Ashrĕ is she who believed, for that which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has said to her shall be accomplished!”
1.46: And Miryam said, “My being makes 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 great,
1.47: and my spirit has rejoiced in Elohim my Savior.
1.48: “Because He looked on the humiliation of His female servant. For look, from now on all generations shall call me fortunate.
1.49: “For He who is mighty has done wonders for me, and qodesh is His Name.
1.50: “And His compassion is from generation to generation, to those who revere Him.
1.51: “He did mightily with His arm, He scattered the proud in the thought of their hearts.
1.52: “He brought down rulers from their thrones, and exalted the lowly.
1.53: “He has filled the hungry with good, and the rich He has sent away empty.
1.54: “He sustained Yisra’ĕl, His servant, in remembrance of His compassion,
1.55: as He spoke to our fathers, to Aḇraham and to his seed, forever.”
1.56: And Miryam stayed with her about three months, and returned to her home.
1.57: And the time was filled for Elisheḇa to give birth, and she bore a son.
1.58: And her neighbors and relatives heard how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had shown great compassion to her, and they rejoiced with her.
1.59: And it came to be, on the eighth day, that they came to circumcise the child. And they were calling him by the name of his father, Zeḵaryah.
1.60: And his mother answering, said, “Not so, but he shall be called Yoḥanan.”
1.61: And they said to her, “There is no one among your relatives who is called by this name.”
1.62: Then they motioned to his father, what he would like him to be called.
1.63: And having asked for a writing tablet, he wrote, saying, “Yoḥanan is his name.” And they all marveled.
1.64: And at once his mouth was opened and his tongue loosed, and he was speaking, baraḵ Elohim.
1.65: And fear came on all those dwelling around them, and all these matters were spoken of in all the hill country of Yahuḏah.
1.66: And all who heard them kept them in their hearts, saying, “What then shall this child be?” And the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was with him.
1.67: And Zeḵaryah, his father, was filled with the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, and naḇu, saying,
1.68: “Baruḵ be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, for He looked upon and worked redemption for His people,
1.69: and has raised up a horn of deliverance for us in the house of His servant Dawiḏ,
1.70: as He spoke by the mouth of His qodesh neḇi’im, from of old -
1.71: deliverance from our enemies and from the hand of all those hating us,
1.72: to show compassion toward our fathers and to remember His qodesh Covenant,
1.73: an oath which He swore to our father Aḇraham:
1.74: to give to us, being delivered from the hand of our enemies, to serve Him without fear,
1.75: in qodeshah and righteousness before Him all the days of our life.
1.76: “And you, child, shall be called naḇi of the Most High, for you shall go before the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to prepare His ways,
1.77: to give knowledge of deliverance to His people, by the forgiveness of their sins,
1.78: through the tender compassion of our Elohim, with which the daybreak from on high has looked upon us,
1.79: to give light to those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.”
1.80: And the child grew and became strong in spirit, and was in the deserts until the day of showing Himself openly to Yisra’ĕl.

10.1: And after this the Aḏon appointed seventy others, and sent them two by two ahead of Him into every city and place where He Himself was about to go.
10.2: Then He said to them, “The harvest indeed is great, but the workers are few, therefore pray to the Aḏon of the harvest to send out workers into His harvest.
10.3: “Go! See, I send you out as lambs into the midst of wolves.
10.4: “Do not take a purse, nor a bag, nor sandals. And greet no one along the way.
10.5: “And whatever house you enter, first say, ‘Peace to this house.’
10.6: “And if indeed a son of peace is there, your peace shall rest on it; and if not, it shall return to you.
10.7: “And stay in the same house, eating and drinking what they provide, for the laborer is worthy of his wages. Do not move from house to house.
10.8: “And into whatever city you enter, and they receive you, eat whatever is placed before you,
10.9: and heal the sick there, and say to them, ‘The Malḵuth of Elohim has come near to you.’
10.10: “And into whatever city you enter, and they do not receive you, go out into its streets and say,
10.11: ‘Even the dust of your city which clings to us, we wipe off against you, but know this, that the Malḵuth of Elohim has come near to you.’
10.12: “And I say to you that it shall be more bearable for Seḏom in that Day, than for that city.
10.13: “Woe to you, Ḵorazin! Woe to you, Bĕyth Tsaiḏa! For if the miracles which were done in you had been done in Tsor and Tsiḏon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
10.14: “But it shall be more bearable for Tsor and Tsiḏon at the judgment than for you.
10.15: “And you, Kephar Naḥum, who are exalted to the shamayim, shall be brought down to the grave.
10.16: “He who hears you hears Me, he who rejects you rejects Me, and he who rejects Me rejects Him who sent Me.”
10.17: And the seventy returned with joy, saying, “Aḏonai, even the demons are subject to us in Your Name.”
10.18: And He said to them, “I saw Satan falling out of the shamayim as lightning.
10.19: “See, I give you the authority to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and none at all shall hurt you.
10.20: “But do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rather rejoice because your names have been written in the shamayim.”
10.21: In that hour 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 exulted in the Ruaḥ and said, “I praise You, Father, Aḏon of the shamayim and of the earth, that You have hidden these from clever and learned ones, and revealed them to children. Yes, Father, because thus it was well-pleasing in Your sight.
10.22: “All has been delivered to Me by My Father, and no one knows who the Bĕn is, except the Father, and who the Father is, except the Bĕn, and he to whom the Bĕn wants to reveal.”
10.23: And turning to His talmidim He said, separately, “Ashrĕ are the eyes that see what you see,
10.24: for I say to you that many neḇi’im and melaḵim have wanted to see what you see, and have not seen it, and to hear what you hear, and have not heard it.”
10.25: And see, a certain one learned in the Torah stood up, trying Him, and saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit everlasting ḥai?”
10.26: And He said to him, “What has been written in the Torah? How do you read it?”
10.27: And he answering, said, “ ‘You shall love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim with all your heart, and with all your being, and with all your strength, and with all your mind,’ and ‘your neighbor as yourself.’ ”
10.28: And He said to him, “You have answered rightly. Do this and you shall live.”
10.29: But he, wanting to declare himself righteous, said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, “And who is my neighbor?”
10.30: And replying, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said, “A certain man was going down from Yerushalayim to Yeriḥo, and fell among robbers, who, both stripping and beating him, went away, leaving him half dead.
10.31: “And by a coincidence a certain kohĕn was going down that way. And when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
10.32: “And likewise a Lĕwite also, when he came to the place, and seeing, passed by on the other side.
10.33: “But a certain Shomeronite, journeying, came upon him. And when he saw him, he had compassion on him,
10.34: and he went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. And having placed him on his own beast, he brought him to an inn, and looked after him.
10.35: “And going out on the next day, he took out two pieces of silver, gave them to the innkeeper, and said to him, ‘Look after him, and whatever more you spend I shall repay you when I return.’
10.36: “Who, then, of these three, do you think, was neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?”
10.37: And he said, “He who showed compassion on him.” Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “Go and do likewise.”
10.38: And it came to be as they went that He entered into a certain village. And a certain woman named Martha received Him into her house.
10.39: And she had a sister called Miryam, who also sat at the feet of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 and heard His Word.
10.40: But Martha was distracted with much serving, and coming up she said, “Aḏonai, are You not concerned that my sister has left me to serve alone? Speak to her then, to help me.”
10.41: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answering, said to her, “Martha, Martha, you are worried and troubled about much,
10.42: but one only is necessary, and Miryam has chosen the good portion, which shall not be taken away from her.”

11.1: And it came to be while He was praying in a certain place, as He ceased, one of His talmidim said to Him, “Aḏonai, teach us to pray, as Yoḥanan also taught his talmidim.”
11.2: And He said to them, “When you pray, say: Our Father in the shamayim, let Your Name be qodesh, let Your Malḵuth come, let Your desire be done on earth as it is in shamayim.
11.3: “Give us day by day our daily bread.
11.4: “And forgive us our sins, for we also forgive everyone who is indebted to us. And do not lead us into trial, but rescue us from the wicked one.”
11.5: And He said to them, “Which of you shall have a friend, and go to him at midnight and say to him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves,
11.6: since a friend of mine has come to me on his journey, and I have naught to put before him,’
11.7: then the one inside answering, says, ‘Do not trouble me, the door is already locked, and my children with me are in bed. I am unable to get up and give to you’?
11.8: “I say to you, if he does not get up and give to him because he is his friend, he shall get up and give him as many as he needs because of his persistence.
11.9: “And I say to you: ask and it shall be given to you, seek and you shall find, knock and it shall be opened to you.
11.10: “For everyone asking receives, and he who is seeking finds, and to him who is knocking it shall be opened.
11.11: “And what father among you whose son asks for bread shall give him a stone, or if he asks for a fish shall give him a snake instead of a fish,
11.12: or if he asks for an egg shall give him a scorpion?
11.13: “If you then, being wicked, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more shall your Father from shamayim give the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh to those asking Him!”
11.14: And He was casting out a demon, and it was dumb. And it came to be, when the demon had gone out, that the dumb spoke. And the crowds marveled.
11.15: But some of them said, “He casts out demons by Be’elzebul, the ruler of the demons,”
11.16: and others, trying, were seeking from Him a sign from the shamayim.
11.17: And He, knowing their thoughts, said to them, “Every malḵuth divided against itself is laid waste, and a house against a house falls.
11.18: “So if Satan also is divided against himself, how shall his malḵuth stand? Because you say I cast out demons by Be’elzebul.
11.19: “Now if I cast out demons by Be’elzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Because of this they shall be your judges.
11.20: “But if I cast out demons by the finger of Elohim, then the Malḵuth of Elohim has come upon you.
11.21: “When a strong man, having been well armed, watches over his own court, his possessions are in peace.
11.22: “But when a stronger than he comes upon him and overcomes him, he takes from him all his armor in which he trusted, and divides his booty.
11.23: “He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters.
11.24: “When the unclean spirit goes out of a man, he goes through dry places, seeking rest. And finding none, he says, ‘I shall return to my house from which I came.’
11.25: “And when he comes, he finds it swept and decorated,
11.26: then he goes and takes with him seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter and dwell there. And the last of that man becomes worse than the first.”
11.27: And it came to be, as He was saying this, a certain woman from the crowd raised her voice and said to Him, “Ashrĕ is the womb that bore You, and the breasts which You nursed on!”
11.28: But He said, “Ashrĕ rather are those hearing the Word of Elohim and keeping it!”
11.29: And while the crowds were thronging, He began to say, “This generation is wicked. It seeks a sign, and no sign shall be given to it except the sign of Yonah the naḇi.
11.30: “For as Yonah became a sign to the Ninewites, so also the Bĕn of Aḏam shall be to this generation.
11.31: “The malkah of the South shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation and shall condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Shelomoh, and look, a greater than Shelomoh is here.
11.32: “The men of Ninewĕh shall rise up in the judgment with this generation and condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Yonah, and look, a greater than Yonah is here.
11.33: “And no one, when he has lit a lamp, puts it in a hidden place or under a basket, but on a lampstand, that those who come in shall see the light.
11.34: “The lamp of the body is the eye. Therefore, when your eye is good, all your body also is enlightened. But when your eye is evil, your body also is darkened.
11.35: “See to it therefore that the light which is in you is not darkness.
11.36: “If then all your body is enlightened, having no part dark, all shall be enlightened, as when the bright shining of a lamp gives you light.”
11.37: And as He spoke, a certain Pharisee asked Him to dine with him, so He went in and sat down to eat.
11.38: And when the Pharisee saw it, he marveled that He did not first wash before dinner.
11.39: And the Aḏon said to him, “Now you Pharisees make the outside of the cup and dish clean, but your inward part is filled with greed and wickedness.
11.40: “Mindless ones! Did not He who made the outside make the inside also?
11.41: “But give in kindness of that which is within, and see, all are clean to you.
11.42: “But woe to you Pharisees, because you tithe the mint and the rue and every plant, and pass by the right-ruling and the love of Elohim. These you should have done, without leaving the others undone.
11.43: “Woe to you Pharisees, because you love the best seats in the congregations and the greetings in the market-places.
11.44: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like the unseen tombs, and the men walking over them do not know.”
11.45: And one of those learned in the Torah, answering, said to Him, “Teacher, when You say this You insult us too.”
11.46: And He said, “Woe to you also, you learned in the Torah, because you load men with burdens hard to bear, and you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.
11.47: “Woe to you, because you build the tombs of the neḇi’im, and your fathers killed them.
11.48: “So you bear witness that you approve of the works of your fathers, because they indeed killed them, and you build their tombs.
11.49: “And because of this the wisdom of Elohim said, ‘I shall send them neḇi’im and emissaries, and some of them they shall kill and persecute,’
11.50: so that the blood of all the neḇi’im which was shed from the foundation of the world shall be required of this generation,
11.51: from the blood of Heḇel to the blood of Zeḵaryah who perished between the altar and the Mishkan. Yes, I say to you, it shall be required of this generation.
11.52: “Woe to you learned in the Torah, because you took away the key of knowledge. You did not enter in yourselves, and those who were entering in you hindered.”
11.53: And as He was saying this to them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to oppose Him fiercely, and to draw Him out on many subjects,
11.54: watching Him, and seeking to catch somewhat from His mouth, so as to accuse Him.

12.1: Meanwhile, when an innumerable crowd of people had gathered together, so that they trampled one another, He began to say to His talmidim, first, “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
12.2: “And whatever is concealed shall be revealed, and whatever is hidden shall be known.
12.3: “So, whatever you have said in the dark shall be heard in the light, and what you have spoken in the ear in inner rooms shall be proclaimed on the house-tops.
12.4: “But I say to you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body, and after that are unable to do any more.
12.5: “But I shall show you whom you should fear: Fear the One who, after killing, possesses authority to cast into Gĕy-Hinnom. Yes, I say to you, fear Him!
12.6: “Are not five sparrows sold for two copper coins? And not one of them is forgotten before Elohim.
12.7: “But even the hairs of your head have all been numbered. Do not fear, you are worth more than many sparrows.
12.8: “And I say to you, everyone who confesses Me before men, the Bĕn of Aḏam shall also confess him before the messengers of Elohim.
12.9: “But he that has denied Me before men shall be denied before the messengers of Elohim.
12.10: “And everyone who shall speak a word against the Bĕn of Aḏam, it shall be forgiven him, but to him who has blasphemed against the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, it shall not be forgiven.
12.11: “And when they bring you to the congregations and rulers and authorities, do not worry about how or what you should answer, or what you should say,
12.12: for the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh shall teach you in that very hour what you should say.”
12.13: And someone from the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, speak to my brother, to divide the inheritance with me.”
12.14: But He said to him, “Man, who made Me a judge or divider over you?”
12.15: And He said to them, “Mind, and beware of greed, because one’s life does not consist in the excess of his possessions.”
12.16: He then spoke a parable to them, saying, “The land of a certain rich man yielded well.
12.17: “And he was reasoning within himself, saying, ‘What shall I do, because I have no room to store my crops?’
12.18: “And he said, ‘I am going to do this: pull down my storehouses and build greater, and store all my crops and my goods there,
12.19: then say to myself, “Life, you have many goods laid up for many years, take your ease, eat, drink, rejoice.” ’
12.20: “But Elohim said to him, ‘You mindless one! This night your life shall be demanded from you. And who shall own what you have prepared?’
12.21: “So is he who is storing up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward Elohim.”
12.22: And He said to His talmidim, “For this reason I say to you, do not worry about your life, what you shall eat; nor about the body, what you shall put on.
12.23: “The life is more than the food, and the body is more than the clothing.
12.24: “Look at the ravens, for they neither sow nor reap, which have neither storehouse nor granary, and Elohim feeds them. How much more valuable are you than the birds?
12.25: “And which of you by worrying is able to add one pĕḵus to his life’s span?
12.26: “If then you are unable to do the least, why do you worry about the rest?
12.27: “Look at the lilies, how they grow. They neither toil nor spin, and I say to you, even Shelomoh in all his esteem was not dressed like one of these.
12.28: “And if Elohim so clothes the grass, which today exists in the field and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, how much more you, O you of little belief?
12.29: “And do not seek what you shall eat or what you shall drink, and do not keep worrying.
12.30: “For the gentiles of the world seek all these, and your Father knows that you need these.
12.31: “But seek the Malḵuth of Elohim, and all these shall be added to you.
12.32: “Do not fear, little flock, because your Father delights to give you the Malḵuth.
12.33: “Sell your possessions and give in kindness. Make yourselves purses which do not grow old, a treasure in the shamayim that does not fail, where no thief comes near nor moth destroys.
12.34: “For where your treasure is, there your heart shall be also.
12.35: “Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning,
12.36: and be like men waiting for their master, when he shall return from the wedding, that when he comes and knocks they open to him immediately.
12.37: “Ashrĕ are those servants whom the master, when he comes, shall find watching. Truly, I say to you that he shall gird himself and make them sit down to eat, and shall come and serve them.
12.38: “And if he comes in the second watch, or in the third watch, and finds them so, ashrĕ are those servants.
12.39: “And know this, that if the master of the house had known what hour the thief comes, he would have watched and not allowed his house to be broken into.
12.40: “And you, then, be ready, for the Bĕn of Aḏam is coming at an hour you do not expect.”
12.41: And Kĕpha said to Him, “Aḏonai, do You speak this parable to us, or also to all?”
12.42: And the Aḏon said, “Who then is the trustworthy and wise manager, whom his master shall appoint over his household, to give the portion of food in due season?
12.43: “Ashrĕ is that servant whom his master shall find so doing when he comes.
12.44: “Truly, I say to you that he shall appoint him over all his possessions.
12.45: “But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My master is delaying his coming,’ and begins to beat the male servants and female servants, and to eat and drink and be drunk,
12.46: the master of that servant shall come on a day when he does not expect him, and at an hour that he does not know, and shall cut him in two and appoint his portion with the unbelievers.
12.47: “And that servant who knew his master’s desire, and did not prepare, nor did according to his desire, shall be beaten much.
12.48: “But he who did not know, yet did what deserved flogging, shall be beaten with few. And everyone to whom much is given, from him much shall be demanded. And to whom much has been entrusted, from him much more shall be asked.
12.49: “I came to send fire on the earth, and how I prefer it were already kindled!
12.50: “But I have an immersion to be immersed with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
12.51: “Do you think that I came to give peace on earth? I say to you, no, but rather division.
12.52: “For from now on five in one house shall be divided, three against two, and two against three -
12.53: father shall be divided against son, and son against father, mother against daughter, and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”
12.54: And He also said to the crowds, “When you see a cloud rising out of the west, immediately you say, ‘A storm is coming,’ and so it is.
12.55: “And when you see the south wind blow, you say, ‘There shall be hot weather,’ and it is.
12.56: “Hypocrites! You know to discern the face of the shamayim and of the earth, but how is it you do not discern this time?
12.57: “And why, also, do you not judge for yourselves what is right?
12.58: “For, as you go with your opponent to a ruler, try hard along the way to settle with him, lest he drag you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
12.59: “I say to you, you shall certainly not leave there until you have paid even the last coin.”

13.1: And some were present at that time, reporting to Him about the Galileans whose blood Pilatus had mixed with their offerings.
13.2: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answering, said to them, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all Galileans, because they have suffered like this?
13.3: “I say to you, no! But unless you repent you shall all perish in the same way.
13.4: “Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Shiloaḥ fell and killed them, do you think that they were greater offenders than all other men who dwelt in Yerushalayim?
13.5: “I say to you, no! But unless you repent you shall all perish in the same way.”
13.6: And He spoke this parable, “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and found none.
13.7: “And he said to the gardener, ‘Look, for three years I have come seeking fruit on this fig tree and find none. Cut it down, why does it even make the ground useless?’
13.8: “And he answering, said to him, ‘Master, leave it this year too, until I dig around it and throw manure.
13.9: ‘And if indeed it bears fruit—but if not so, after that you shall cut it down.’ ”
13.10: And He was teaching in one of the congregations on the Shabbath,
13.11: and see, there was a woman having a weakening spirit for eighteen years, and was bent over and was unable to straighten up at all.
13.12: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, seeing her, called her near and said to her, “Woman, you are loosened from your weakness.”
13.13: And He laid His hands on her, and immediately she was straightened up, and praised Elohim.
13.14: But the ruler of the congregation, responding, much displeased that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 had healed on the Shabbath, said to the crowd, “There are six days on which men should work, so come and be healed on them, and not on the Shabbath day.”
13.15: Then the Aḏon answered him and said, “Hypocrite! Does not each one of you on the Shabbath loosen his ox or his donkey from the stall and lead it away to water it?
13.16: “And this one, being a daughter of Aḇraham, whom Satan has bound, look, for eighteen years, should she not be loosened from this bond on the Shabbath?”
13.17: And when He said this, all His opponents were put to shame. And all the crowd rejoiced for all the splendor being done by Him.
13.18: Therefore He said, “What is the Malḵuth of Elohim like? And to what shall I compare it?
13.19: “It is like a mustard seed, which a man took and threw into his garden. And it grew and became a large tree, and the birds of the shamayim nested in its branches.”
13.20: And again He said, “To what shall I compare the Malḵuth of Elohim?
13.21: “It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until it was all leavened.”
13.22: And He was going through the cities and villages, teaching, and journeying toward Yerushalayim,
13.23: and someone said to Him, “Aḏonai, are there few who are being saved?” And He said to them,
13.24: “Strive to enter through the narrow gate, because many, I say to you, shall seek to enter in and shall not be able.
13.25: “When once the Aḏon of the house has risen up and shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying, ‘Aḏonai, Aḏonai, open for us,’ and He shall answer and say to you, ‘I do not know you, where you are from,’
13.26: then you shall begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in Your presence, and You taught in our streets.’
13.27: “But He shall say, ‘I say to you I do not know you, where you are from. Depart from Me, all you workers of unrighteousness.’
13.28: “There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Aḇraham and Yitsḥaq and Ya’aqoḇ and all the neḇi’im in the Malḵuth of Elohim, and yourselves thrown outside.
13.29: “And they shall come from the east and the west, and from the north and the south, and sit down in the Malḵuth of Elohim.
13.30: “And see, there are last who shall be first, and there are first who shall be last.”
13.31: On the same day there came certain Pharisees, saying to Him, “Get out and go from here, for Hĕrodĕs wants to kill You.”
13.32: And He said to them, “Go, say to that fox, ‘See, I cast out demons and perform healings today and tomorrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.’
13.33: “But I have to journey today, and tomorrow, and the day following, because it is not possible for a naḇi to perish outside of Yerushalayim.
13.34: “Yerushalayim, Yerushalayim, killing the neḇi’im and stoning those who are sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together, the way a hen her chickens under her wings, but you would not!
13.35: “See, your House is left to you laid waste. And truly I say to you, you shall by no means see Me until it comes when you say, ‘Baruḵ is He who is coming in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!’ ”

14.1: And it came to be, as He went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees to eat bread on the Shabbath, that they were watching Him closely.
14.2: And see, there was a certain man before Him suffering from dropsy.
14.3: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 responding, spoke to those learned in the Torah and the Pharisees, saying, “Is it right to heal on the Shabbath?”
14.4: But they were silent. So taking hold of him He healed him, and let him go.
14.5: And to them He said, “Which of you, having a donkey or an ox that has fallen into a pit, shall not immediately pull him out on the Shabbath day?”
14.6: And they were unable to answer Him regarding these.
14.7: And He spoke a parable to those who were invited, when He noted how they chose the best places, saying to them:
14.8: “When you are invited by anyone to a wedding feast, do not sit down in the best place, lest one more distinguished than you be invited by him,
14.9: and he who invited you and him come and say to you, ‘Give this one place,’ and then you begin with shame to take the last place.
14.10: “Rather, when you are invited, go and sit down in the last place, so that when he who invited you comes he shall say to you, ‘Friend, come up higher.’ Then you shall have esteem in the presence of those who sit at the table with you.
14.11: “For everyone who is exalting himself shall be humbled, and he who is humbling himself shall be exalted.”
14.12: And He also said to him who invited Him, “When you give a dinner or a supper, do not ask your friends, nor your brothers, nor your relatives, nor your rich neighbors, lest they also invite you back, and you be repaid.
14.13: “But when you give a feast, invite poor ones, crippled ones, lame ones, blind ones,
14.14: and you shall be ashrĕ because they are unable to repay you. For you shall be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
14.15: And when one of those who sat at the table with Him heard this, he said to Him, “Ashrĕ is he who eats bread in the Malḵuth of Elohim!”
14.16: But He said to him, “A certain man gave a great supper and invited many,
14.17: and he sent his servant at supper time to say to those who were invited, ‘Come, for all is now ready.’
14.18: “But they all alike began making excuses. The first said to him, ‘I have bought a field, and I need to go and see it. I ask you to have me excused.’
14.19: “And another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. I ask you to have me excused.’
14.20: “And another said, ‘I have married a wife, and because of this I am unable to come.’
14.21: “And that servant came and reported this to his master. Then the master of the house, being wroth, said to his servant, ‘Hurry out into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor, and crippled, and lame, and blind.’
14.22: “And the servant said, ‘Master, it is done as you commanded, and still there is room.’
14.23: “And the master said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, so that my house is filled.
14.24: ‘For I say to you that none of those men who were invited shall taste my supper.’ ”
14.25: And large crowds were going with Him, and turning, He said to them,
14.26: “If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father and mother, and wife, and children, and brothers, and sisters, and his own life too, he is unable to be My talmid.
14.27: “And whoever does not bear his stake and come after Me is unable to be My talmid.
14.28: “For who of you, wanting to build a tower, does not sit down first and count the cost, whether his possessions will finish it?
14.29: “Otherwise, when he has laid the foundation, and is unable to finish it, all who see it begin to mock him,
14.30: saying, ‘This man began to build and was unable to finish.’
14.31: “Or what meleḵ, going to fight against another meleḵ, does not sit down first and take counsel whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?
14.32: “And if not, while the other is still far away, he sends a delegation and asks conditions of peace.
14.33: “So, then, every one of you who does not give up all that he has, is unable to be My talmid.
14.34: “The salt is good, but if the salt becomes tasteless, with what shall it be seasoned?
14.35: “It is not fit for land, nor for manure, they throw it out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear!”

15.1: Now all the tax collectors and the sinners were coming to Him to hear Him.
15.2: And the Pharisees and scribes grumbled, saying, “This One receives sinners and eats with them.”
15.3: And He spoke this parable to them, saying,
15.4: “What man among you, having a hundred sheep, and having lost one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one which is lost until he finds it?
15.5: “And having found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
15.6: “And having come home, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’
15.7: “I say to you that in the same way there shall be more joy in the shamayim over one sinner repenting, than over ninety-nine righteous ones who need no repentance.
15.8: “Or what woman, having ten silver coins, if she loses one coin, does not light a lamp and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she finds it?
15.9: “And having found it, she calls friends and neighbors together, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the coin which I lost!’
15.10: “I say to you, in the same way there is joy in the presence of the messengers of Elohim over one sinner repenting.”
15.11: And He said, “A certain man had two sons,
15.12: and the younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me the portion of goods that falls to me.’ And he divided his livelihood between them.
15.13: “And not many days after, the younger son, having gathered all together, went away to a distant country, and there wasted his goods with loose living.
15.14: “And when he had spent all, there arose a severe scarcity of food throughout that land, and he began to be in need.
15.15: “And he went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him to his fields to feed pigs.
15.16: “And he was longing to fill his stomach with the pods which the pigs were eating, and no one gave to him.
15.17: “But having come to himself, he said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have bread enough and to spare, and I am perishing with hunger!
15.18: ‘Having risen, I shall go to my father and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against the shamayim, and before you,
15.19: and I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants.” ’
15.20: “And having risen, he went to his father. And while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran and fell on his neck and kissed him.
15.21: “And the son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against the shamayim, and before you, and I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
15.22: “But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
15.23: ‘And bring the fattened calf here and slaughter it, and let us eat and rejoice,
15.24: because this son of mine was dead and is alive again, and he was lost and is found.’ And they began to rejoice.
15.25: “And his older son was in the field, and when he came and approached the house, he heard music and dancing.
15.26: “And having called one of the servants he asked what this meant.
15.27: “And he said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has slaughtered the fattened calf because he received him back in health.’
15.28: “And he was wroth and would not go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.
15.29: “And answering, he said to his father, ‘See, these many years I have been serving you, and I have never transgressed a command of yours, but to me you have never given a young goat, so I could rejoice with my friends.
15.30: ‘But when this son of yours came, who has devoured your livelihood with whores, you slaughtered the fattened calf for him.’
15.31: “Then he said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me and all I have is yours.
15.32: ‘And we had to rejoice and be glad, for this brother of yours was dead and is alive, and was lost and is found.’ ”

16.1: And He also said to His talmidim, “There was a certain rich man who had a manager and he was accused to him as wasting his possessions.
16.2: “So having called him he said to him, ‘What is this I hear about you? Give an account of your management, for you are no longer able to be manager.’
16.3: “And the manager said within himself, ‘What shall I do? For my master is taking the managership away from me. I am unable to dig, I am ashamed to beg.
16.4: ‘I know what I shall do, that, when I am removed from the managership, they might receive me into their houses.’
16.5: “And calling every one of his master’s debtors to him, he said to the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’
16.6: “And he said, ‘A hundred measures of oil.’ And he said to him, ‘Take your account, and sit down quickly and write fifty.’
16.7: “Then to another he said, ‘And how much do you owe?’ And he said, ‘A hundred measures of wheat.’ And he said to him, ‘Take your account, and write eighty.’
16.8: “And the master praised the unrighteous manager because he had acted shrewdly, because the sons of this age are more shrewd in their generation than the sons of light.
16.9: “And I say to you, make friends for yourselves by unrighteous wealth, that when you fail, they shall receive you into everlasting dwellings.
16.10: “He who is trustworthy in what is least, is trustworthy also in much. And he who is unrighteous in what is least is unrighteous also in much.
16.11: “If, therefore, you have not been trustworthy in the unrighteous wealth, who shall entrust to you the true?
16.12: “And if you have not been trust worthy in what is another man’s, who shall give you what is your own?
16.13: “No servant is able to serve two masters, for either he shall hate the one and love the other, or else he shall cling to the one and despise the other. You are not able to serve Elohim and wealth.”
16.14: And the Pharisees, who loved silver, also heard all this, and were sneering at Him,
16.15: so He said to them, “You are those who declare yourselves righteous before men, but Elohim knows your hearts, because what is highly thought of among men is an abomination in the sight of Elohim.
16.16: “The Torah and the Neḇi’im are until Yoḥanan. Since then the Malḵuth of Elohim is being announced, and everyone is doing violence upon it.
16.17: “And it is easier for the shamayim and the earth to pass away than for one tittle of the Torah to fall.
16.18: “Everyone divorcing his wife and marrying another commits adultery. And everyone marrying her who is divorced from her husband commits adultery.
16.19: “But there was a certain rich man who used to dress in purple and fine linen and lived luxuriously every day.
16.20: “And there was a certain beggar named El’azar, being covered with sores, who was placed at his gate,
16.21: and longing to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table. Indeed, even the dogs came and licked his sores.
16.22: “And it came to be that the beggar died, and was carried by the messengers to the bosom of Aḇraham. And the rich man also died and was buried.
16.23: “And while suffering tortures in the grave, having lifted up his eyes, he saw Aḇraham far away, and El’azar in his bosom.
16.24: “And crying out he said, ‘Father Aḇraham, have compassion on me, and send El’azar to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am suffering in this flame.’
16.25: “But Aḇraham said, ‘Son, remember that in your life you received your good, and likewise El’azar the evil, but now he is comforted and you are suffering.
16.26: ‘And besides all this, between us and you a great chasm has been put, so that those who want to pass from here to you are unable, nor do those from there pass to us.’
16.27: “And he said, ‘Then I beg you, father, that you would send him to my father’s house,
16.28: for I have five brothers, let him warn them, lest they also come to this place of torture.’
16.29: “Aḇraham said to him, ‘They have Mosheh and the Neḇi’im, let them hear them.’
16.30: “And he said, ‘No, father Aḇraham, but if someone from the dead goes to them, they shall repent.’
16.31: “But he said to him, ‘If they do not hear Mosheh and the Neḇi’im, neither would they be persuaded even if one should rise from the dead.’ ”

17.1: And He said to the talmidim, “It is inevitable that stumbling-blocks should come, but woe to him through whom they come!
17.2: “It would be better for him if a millstone is put around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
17.3: “Take heed to yourselves. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him.
17.4: “And if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times in a day comes back to you, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”
17.5: And the emissaries said to the Aḏon, “Give us more belief.”
17.6: And the Aḏon said, “If you have belief as a mustard seed, you would say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be pulled up by the roots and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.
17.7: “But who of you, having a servant ploughing or shepherding, would say to him when he has come in from the field, ‘Come immediately and sit down to eat’?
17.8: “But would he not rather say to him, ‘Prepare somewhat for my supper, and gird yourself and serve me while I eat and drink, and afterward you shall eat and drink’?
17.9: “Would he thank that servant because he did what he was commanded? I think not.
17.10: “So also you, when you have done all that you were commanded, say, ‘We are unworthy servants, we have done what was our duty to do.’ ”
17.11: And it came to be, as He went to Yerushalayim, that He passed through the midst of Shomeron and Galil.
17.12: And as He was entering into a certain village, He was met by ten leprous men, who stood at a distance.
17.13: And they lifted up their voices, saying, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, Aḏonai, have compassion on us!”
17.14: And having seen, He said to them, “Go, show yourselves to the kohenim.” And it came to be, that as they were going, they were cleansed.
17.15: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, returned, praising Elohim with a loud voice,
17.16: and he fell down upon his face at His feet, giving thanks to Him. And he was a Shomeronite.
17.17: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answering, said, “Were there not ten cleansed? But where are the nine?
17.18: “Was no one found to return to give praise to Elohim, except this foreigner?”
17.19: And He said to him, “Rise, go your way. Your belief has made you well.”
17.20: And having been asked by the Pharisees when the Malḵuth of Elohim would come, He answered them and said, “The Malḵuth of Elohim does not come with intent watching,
17.21: nor shall they say, ‘Look here!’ or ‘Look there!’ For look, the Malḵuth of Elohim is in your midst!”
17.22: And He said to the talmidim, “Days shall come when you shall long to see one of the days of the Bĕn of Aḏam, but you shall not see it.
17.23: And they shall say to you, ‘Look here!’ or ‘Look there!’ Do not go after them, nor follow.
17.24: “For as the lightning that flashes out of one part under the shamayim shines to the other part under the shamayim, so also the Bĕn of Aḏam shall be in His day.
17.25: “But first He has to suffer much and be rejected by this generation.
17.26: “And as it came to be in the days of Noaḥ, so also shall it be in the days of the Bĕn of Aḏam:
17.27: “They were eating, they were drinking, they were marrying, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noaḥ went into the ark, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
17.28: “And likewise, as it came to be in the days of Lot: They were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling, they were planting, they were building,
17.29: but on the day Lot went out of Seḏom it rained fire and sulphur from the shamayim and destroyed all.
17.30: “It shall be the same in the day the Bĕn of Aḏam is revealed.
17.31: “In that day, he who shall be on the house-top, and his goods in the house, let him not come down to take them away. And likewise the one who is in the field, let him not turn back.
17.33: “Whoever seeks to save his life shall lose it, and whoever loses his life shall preserve it.
17.34: “I say to you, in that night there shall be two in one bed, the one shall be taken and the other shall be left.
17.35: “Two shall be grinding together, the one shall be taken and the other shall be left.
17.36: “Two shall be in the field, the one shall be taken and the other shall be left.”
17.37: And they answering, said to Him, “Where, Aḏonai?” And He said to them, “Where the body is, there also the vultures shall be gathered together.”

18.1: And He spoke a parable to them, that they should always pray and not lose heart,
18.2: saying, “In a certain city there was a certain judge, not revering Elohim nor regarding man.
18.3: “And a widow was in that city, and she came to him, saying, ‘Do right to me on my adversary.’
18.4: “And he would not for a while, but afterward he said within himself, ‘Even if I do not revere Elohim nor regard man,
18.5: yet because this widow troubles me I shall do right to her, lest by her continual coming she wears me out.’ ”
18.6: And the Aḏon said, “Hear what the unrighteous judge said.
18.7: “And shall Elohim not do right by all means to His own chosen ones who are crying out day and night to Him, and being patient over them?
18.8: “I say to you that He shall do right to them speedily. But when the Bĕn of Aḏam comes, shall He find the belief on the earth?”
18.9: And He also spoke this parable to some who relied on themselves that they were righteous, and looking down on others:
18.10: “Two men went up to the Miqdash to pray - the one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
18.11: “The Pharisee stood and began to pray with himself this way, ‘Elohim, I thank You that I am not like the rest of men, swindlers, unrighteous, adulterers, or even as this tax collector.
18.12: ‘I fast twice a week, I give tithes of all that I possess.’
18.13: “But the tax collector standing at a distance would not even raise his eyes to the shamayim, but was beating his breast, saying, ‘Elohim, show favor unto me, a sinner!’
18.14: “I say to you, this man went down to his house declared right, rather than the other. For everyone who is exalting himself shall be humbled, and he who is humbling himself shall be exalted.”
18.15: And they also brought infants to Him to touch them, but His talmidim seeing it, rebuked them.
18.16: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 called them to Him and said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not forbid them, for of such is the Malḵuth of Elohim.
18.17: “Truly, I say to you, whoever does not receive the Malḵuth of Elohim as a little child, shall certainly not enter into it.”
18.18: And a certain ruler asked Him, saying, “Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit everlasting ḥai?”
18.19: So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good except One - Elohim.
18.20: “You know the Commands, ‘Do not commit adultery,’ ‘Do not murder,’ ‘Do not steal,’ ‘Do not bear false witness,’ ‘Respect your father and your mother.’ ”
18.21: And he said, “All these I have watched over from my youth.”
18.22: And hearing this, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “Yet one you lack: Sell all that you have and distribute to the poor, and you shall have treasure in the shamayim. And come, follow Me.”
18.23: But when he heard this, he became intensely sad, for he was extremely rich.
18.24: And when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 saw that he became intensely sad, He said, “How hard it is for those who have riches to enter into the Malḵuth of Elohim!
18.25: “For it is easier for a camel to enter through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into the Malḵuth of Elohim.”
18.26: And those who heard it said, “And who is able to be saved?”
18.27: And He said, “What is impossible with men is possible with Elohim.”
18.28: And Kĕpha said, “See, we have left all and followed You.”
18.29: And He said to them, “Truly, I say to you, there is no one who has left house or parents or brothers or wife or children, for the sake of the Malḵuth of Elohim,
18.30: who shall not receive many times more in this present time, and in the age to come everlasting ḥai.”
18.31: And taking the twelve aside, He said to them, “See, we are going up to Yerushalayim, and all that have been written by the neḇi’im about the Bĕn of Aḏam shall be accomplished.
18.32: “For He shall be delivered up to the gentiles and shall be mocked and insulted and spat upon,
18.33: and having flogged Him they shall kill Him. And on the third day He shall rise again.”
18.34: But they understood none of this, and this word was hidden from them, and they did not know what was being said.
18.35: And it came to be, that as He was coming near Yeriḥo, that a certain blind man was sitting by the way begging.
18.36: And hearing a crowd passing by, he asked what it meant.
18.37: And they reported to him that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 of Natsareth was passing by.
18.38: And he cried out, saying, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, Bĕn of Dawiḏ, have compassion on me!”
18.39: And those going before were rebuking him that he should be silent, but he was crying out much more, “Bĕn of Dawiḏ, have compassion on me!”
18.40: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 stopped and commanded him to be brought to Him. And when he had come near, He asked him,
18.41: saying, “What do you want Me to do for you?” And he said, “Aḏonai, to receive my sight.”
18.42: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “Receive your sight! Your belief has saved you.”
18.43: And immediately he received his sight, and was following Him, praising Elohim. And all the people, seeing it, gave praise to Elohim.

19.1: And having entered, He was passing through Yeriḥo.
19.2: And see, a man called Zakkai! And he was a chief tax collector, and he was rich,
19.3: and he was seeking to see who 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was, but was unable because of the crowd, for he was small in stature.
19.4: And having run ahead, he climbed up into a sycamore tree to see Him, because He was about to pass by.
19.5: And as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 came to the place, He looked up and saw him, and said to him, “Zakkai, hurry and come down, for I have to stay at your house today.”
19.6: And he hurried and came down, and received Him, rejoicing.
19.7: And seeing it, they all grumbled, saying, “He has gone in to stay with a man who is a sinner.”
19.8: But Zakkai stood up and said to the Aḏon, “Look, Aḏonai, I give half of my possessions to the poor. And if I have taken whatever from anyone by false accusation, I repay fourfold.”
19.9: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “Today deliverance has come to this house - since he also is a son of Aḇraham.
19.10: “For the Bĕn of Aḏam has come to seek and to save what was lost.”
19.11: And as they were hearing this, He spoke another parable, because He was near Yerushalayim and they thought the Malḵuth of Elohim was about to be manifested straightaway.
19.12: He therefore said, “A certain nobleman went to a distant country to receive for himself a malḵuth and to return.
19.13: “And calling ten of his servants, He gave them ten minas, and said to them, ‘Trade until I come.’
19.14: “But his subjects were hating him, and sent a delegation after him, to say, ‘We do not want this one to reign over us.’
19.15: “And it came to be, when he came back, having received the malḵuth, that he sent for these servants to whom he had given the silver, in order to know what each had gained by trading.
19.16: “And the first came, saying, ‘Master, your mina has earned ten minas.’
19.17: “And he said to him, ‘Well done, good servant. Because you were trustworthy in very little, have authority over ten cities.’
19.18: “And the second came, saying, ‘Master, your mina has earned five minas.’
19.19: “And he said to him also, ‘And you - be over five cities.’
19.20: “And another came, saying, ‘Master, here is your mina, which I kept laid up in a handkerchief.
19.21: ‘For I was afraid of you, because you are a hard man. You take up what you did not lay down, and reap what you did not sow.’
19.22: “And he said to him, ‘Out of your own mouth I shall judge you, you wicked servant. You knew that I was a hard man, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow.
19.23: ‘Why did you not put my silver in the bank, that when I come I could have collected it with interest?’
19.24: “Then he said to those who stood by, ‘Take the mina from him, and give it to him who possesses ten minas.’
19.25: “But they said to him, ‘Master, he possesses ten minas.’
19.26: ‘For I say to you, that to everyone who possesses shall be given; and from him who does not possess, even what he possesses shall be taken away from him.
19.27: ‘But those enemies of mine who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and slay them before me.’ ”
19.28: And having said this, He went on ahead, going up to Yerushalayim.
19.29: And it came to be, when He came near to Bĕyth Phaḡi and Bĕyth Anyah, at the mountain of Olives, that He sent two of His talmidim,
19.30: saying, “Go into the village opposite you, in which, as you enter, you shall find a colt tied, on which no one has ever sat. Loosen it and bring it here.
19.31: “And if anyone asks you, ‘Why do you loosen it?’ thus you shall say to him, ‘Because the Aḏon has need of it.’ ”
19.32: And those who were sent went away and found it as He had said to them.
19.33: And as they were loosing the colt, the owners of it said to them, “Why do you loosen the colt?”
19.34: And they said, “The Aḏon needs it.”
19.35: So they brought it to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏. And throwing their garments on the colt, they put 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 on it.
19.36: And as He went, they were spreading their garments on the way.
19.37: And as He was coming near, already at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the entire crowd of the talmidim began, to praise Elohim, rejoicing with a loud voice for all the miracles they had seen,
19.38: saying, “ ‘Baruḵ is the Meleḵ who is coming in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!’ Peace in the shamayim and esteem in the highest!”
19.39: And some of the Pharisees from the crowd, said to Him, “Teacher, rebuke Your talmidim.”
19.40: But He answering, said to them, “I say to you that if these shall be silent, the stones would cry out.”
19.41: And as He came near, He saw the city and wept over it,
19.42: saying, “If you only knew even today, these for your peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes.
19.43: “Because days shall come upon you when your enemies shall build a rampart around you, and surround you and press you on all sides,
19.44: and dash you to the ground, and your children within you. And they shall not leave in you one stone upon another, because you did not know the time of your visitation.”
19.45: And having entered into the Miqdash, He began to drive out those selling and buying in it,
19.46: saying to them, “It has been written, ‘My House is a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a ‘den of robbers.’ ”
19.47: And He was teaching daily in the Miqdash. But the chief kohenim, and the scribes, and the leaders of the people were seeking to destroy Him,
19.48: but they did not find what they might do, for all the people were hanging upon Him, listening.

2.1: And it came to be in those days that a decree went out from Kaisar Augustus for all the world to be registered.
2.2: This took place as a first registration while Quirinius was governing Suria.
2.3: And all were going to be registered, each one to his own city.
2.4: And Yosĕph also went up from Galil, out of the city of Natsareth to Yahuḏah, to the city of Dawiḏ, which is called Bĕyth Leḥem, because he was of the house and lineage of Dawiḏ,
2.5: to be registered with Miryam, who was engaged to him - being pregnant.
2.6: And it came to be, that while they were there, the days were filled for her to give birth.
2.7: And she gave birth to her first-born Bĕn, and wrapped Him up, and laid Him down in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in a lodging place.
2.8: And in the same country there were shepherds living out in the fields, keeping watch over their flock by night.
2.9: And look, a messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 stood before them, and the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shone around them, and they were greatly afraid.
2.10: And the messenger said to them, “Do not be afraid, for look, I bring you good news of great joy which shall be to all people.
2.11: “Because there was born to you today in the city of Dawiḏ a Savior, who is ha’Mashiaḥ, the Aḏon.
2.12: “And this is the sign to you: You shall find an infant wrapped up, lying in a feeding trough.”
2.13: And suddenly there was with the messenger a crowd of the host of the shamayim praising Elohim and saying,
2.14: “Esteem to Elohim in the highest, and on earth peace among men with whom He is pleased!”
2.15: And it came to be, when the messengers had gone away from them into the shamayim, that the shepherds said to each other, “Indeed, let us go to Bĕyth Leḥem and see this matter that has taken place, which the Aḏon has made known to us.”
2.16: And they came in haste and found Miryam and Yosĕph, and the infant lying in a feeding trough.
2.17: And having seen, they made known the matter which was spoken to them concerning the child.
2.18: And all those who heard marveled at what the shepherds said to them.
2.19: But Miryam kept all these matters, considering them in her heart.
2.20: And the shepherds returned, esteeming and praising Elohim for all they had heard and seen, as it was spoken to them.
2.21: And when eight days were completed for Him to be circumcised, His Name was called 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, the Name given by the messenger before He was conceived in the womb.
2.22: And when the days of her cleansing according to the Torah of Mosheh were completed, they brought Him to Yerushalayim to present Him to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 -
2.23: as it has been written in the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Every male who opens the womb shall be called qodesh to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄” -
2.24: and to give an offering according to what is said in the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”
2.25: And see, there was a man in Yerushalayim whose name was Shim’on, and this man was righteous and dedicated, looking for the comforting of Yisra’ĕl. And the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh was upon him.
2.26: And it had been revealed to him by the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh that he would not see death before he sees ha’Mashiaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.27: And he came in the Ruaḥ into the Miqdash. And as the parents brought in the Child 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, to do for Him according to the usual practice of the Torah,
2.28: then he took Him up in his arms and baraḵ Elohim and said,
2.29: “Now You are letting Your servant go in peace, O Aḏonai, according to Your word,
2.30: for my eyes have seen Your deliverance,
2.31: which You have prepared before the face of all the peoples,
2.32: a light for the unveiling of the gentiles, and the esteem of Your people Yisra’ĕl.”
2.33: And Yosĕph and His mother were marveling at what was said about Him.
2.34: And Shim’on baraḵ them, and said to Miryam His mother, “See, this One is appointed for a fall and rising of many in Yisra’ĕl, and for a sign spoken against -
2.35: and a sword shall pierce through your own being also - so as to reveal the thoughts of many hearts.”
2.36: And there was Ḥannah, a neḇiyah, a daughter of Penu’ĕl, of the tribe of Ashĕr. She was advanced in years, and had lived with a husband seven years from her maidenhood,
2.37: and she was a widow of about eighty-four years, who did not leave the Miqdash, but served Elohim with fastings and prayers night and day.
2.38: And she, coming in at that moment, gave thanks to Elohim, and spoke of Him to all who were waiting for redemption in Yerushalayim.
2.39: And when they had accomplished all according to the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, they returned to Galil, to their city Natsareth.
2.40: And the Child grew and became strong in spirit, being filled with wisdom. And the favor of Elohim was upon Him.
2.41: And His parents went to Yerushalayim every year at the Festival of the Pesaḥ.
2.42: And when He was twelve years old, they went up to Yerushalayim according to the practice of the Festival.
2.43: When they had accomplished the days, as they returned, the Child 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 stayed behind in Yerushalayim. And His parents did not know it,
2.44: but thinking He was in the company, they went a day’s journey, and were seeking Him among the relatives and friends.
2.45: And not having found Him, they returned to Yerushalayim, seeking Him.
2.46: And it came to be, after three days, that they found Him in the Miqdash, sitting in the midst of the teachers, both listening to them and asking them questions.
2.47: And all who heard Him were astonished at His understanding and answers.
2.48: And having seen Him, they were amazed. And His mother said to Him, “Bĕn, why have You done this to us? See, Your father and I have been anxiously seeking You.”
2.49: And He said to them, “Why were you seeking Me? Did you not know that I had to be at that of My Father?”
2.50: But they did not understand the word which He spoke to them.
2.51: And He went down with them and came to Natsareth, and was subject to them, but His mother kept all these matters in her heart.
2.52: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with Elohim and men.

20.1: And it came to be, on one of those days, as He was teaching the people in the Miqdash and bringing the Good News, that the chief kohenim and the scribes, together with the elders, came up
20.2: and spoke to Him, saying, “Say to us, by what authority are You doing these? Or who is he who gave You this authority?”
20.3: And He answering, said to them, “I shall ask you one question too, and answer Me:
20.4: “The immersion of Yoḥanan - was it from the shamayim or from men?”
20.5: And they debated among themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From the shamayim,’ He shall say, ‘Then why did you not believe him?’
20.6: “But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people shall stone us, for they are persuaded that Yoḥanan was a naḇi.”
20.7: And they answered that they did not know from where it was.
20.8: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Neither do I say to you by what authority I do these.”
20.9: And He began to speak this parable to the people, “A certain man planted a vineyard, and leased it to farmers, and went away for a long time.
20.10: “And in due time he sent a servant to the farmers, to give him some of the fruit of the vineyard. But the farmers beat him and sent him away empty­handed.
20.11: “And again he sent another servant. And they beat him too and maltreated him, and sent him away empty­handed.
20.12: “And again he sent a third. And they wounded him too and cast him out.
20.13: “And the owner of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I shall send my son, the beloved. They might respect him when they see him.’
20.14: “But when the farmers saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, so that the inheritance becomes ours.’
20.15: “And they cast him out of the vineyard and killed him. What, then, shall the owner of the vineyard do to them?
20.16: “He shall come and destroy those farmers and give the vineyard to others.” And having heard, they said, “Let it not be!”
20.17: But He looked at them and said, “What then is this that has been written, ‘The stone which the builders rejected has become the chief corner­stone’?
20.18: “Everyone who falls on that stone shall be broken, but on whomever it falls, he shall be pulverized.”
20.19: And the chief kohenim and the scribes sought to lay hands on Him in the same hour, but they feared the people, for they knew that He had spoken this parable against them.
20.20: And keeping a close watch, they sent spies who pretended to be righteous, to catch Him in a word, in order to deliver Him to the rule and to the authority of the governor.
20.21: So they asked Him, saying, “Teacher, we know that You say and teach rightly, and You are not partial to any, but teach the Way of Elohim truly.
20.22: “Is it right for us to pay taxes to Kaisar or not?”
20.23: But perceiving their craftiness, He said to them, “Why do you try Me?
20.24: “Show Me a silver piece. Whose likeness and inscription does it have?” And they answering, said, “Kaisar’s.”
20.25: And He said to them, “Then give to Kaisar what is Kaisar’s, and to Elohim what is Elohim’s.”
20.26: And they were unable to catch Him in a saying in the presence of the people, and marveling at His answer, they were silent.
20.27: And some of the Sadducees, who deny that there is a resurrection, came to Him and asked Him,
20.28: saying, “Teacher, Mosheh wrote to us that if a man’s brother dies, having a wife, and he dies childless, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
20.29: “Now, there were seven brothers, and the first took a wife, and died childless.
20.30: “And the second took her as wife, and he died childless.
20.31: “And the third took her, and in the same way the seven also. And they left no children, and died.
20.32: “And last of all the woman died too.
20.33: “At the resurrection, then, whose wife does she become? For the seven had her as wife.”
20.34: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answering, said to them, “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage,
20.35: but those who are counted worthy of attaining that age, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are they given in marriage,
20.36: for neither is it possible for them to die any more, because they are like messengers and are sons of Elohim, being sons of the resurrection.
20.37: “But that the dead are raised, even Mosheh showed at the bush when he called 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 ‘the Elohim of Aḇraham, and the Elohim of Yitsḥaq, and the Elohim of Ya’aqoḇ.’
20.38: “Now He is not the Elohim of the dead, but of the living, for all live to Him.”
20.39: And some of the scribes answering, said, “Teacher, You have spoken well.”
20.40: And they dared not question Him anymore.
20.41: And He said to them, “How do they say that ha’Mashiaḥ is the Bĕn of Dawiḏ?
20.42: “For Dawiḏ himself said in the Book of Tehillim, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Aḏoni, “sit at My right hand,
20.43: until I make Your enemies a footstool of Your feet.” ’
20.44: “Dawiḏ then calls Him ‘Aḏoni,’ how is He then his Bĕn?”
20.45: And in the hearing of all the people, He said to His talmidim,
20.46: “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the market-places, and the best seats in the congregations, and the best places at feasts,
20.47: who devour widows’ houses, and for a show make long prayers. They shall receive greater judgment.”

21.1: And looking up He saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury,
21.2: and He saw a certain poor widow putting in two small coins.
21.3: And He said, “Truly I say to you that this poor widow has put in more than all.
21.4: “For all these out of their excess have put in offerings for Elohim, but she out of her poverty has put in all that she had to live on.”
21.5: And as some were speaking about the Miqdash, that it was adorned with pleasant stones and gifts, He said,
21.6: “These that you see - the days are coming in which not one stone shall be left upon another that shall not be thrown down.”
21.7: And they asked Him, saying, “Teacher, but when shall this be? And what is the sign when this is about to take place?”
21.8: And He said, “See that you are not led astray, for many shall come in My Name, saying, ‘I am,’ and, ‘The time is near.’ Then do not go after them.
21.9: “But when you hear of fightings and unrests, do not be alarmed, for these have to take place first, but the end is not immediately.”
21.10: Then He said to them, “Nation shall rise against nation, and malḵuth against malḵuth.
21.11: “And there shall be great earthquakes in various places, and scarcities of food and deadly diseases. And there shall be terrors, and great signs from the shamayim.
21.12: “But before all this, they shall lay their hands on you and persecute you, delivering you up to the congregations and prisons, and be brought before melaḵim and rulers for My Name’s sake.
21.13: “And it shall turn out to you for a witness.
21.14: “Therefore, resolve in your hearts not to premeditate on what to answer.
21.15: “For I shall give you a mouth and wisdom which all your adversaries shall not be able to refute or resist.
21.16: “And you shall also be betrayed by parents and brothers and relatives and friends. And some of you shall be put to death.
21.17: “And you shall be hated by all because of My Name.
21.18: “But not a hair of your head shall be lost at all.
21.20: “And when you see Yerushalayim surrounded by armies, then know that its laying waste is near.
21.21: “Then let those in Yahuḏah flee to the mountains, and let those who are in the midst of her go out, and let not those who are in the fields enter her.
21.22: “Because these are days of vengeance, to fill all that have been written.
21.23: “And woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing children in those days! For there shall be great distress in the earth and wrath upon this people.
21.24: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and be led away captive into all nations. And Yerushalayim shall be trampled underfoot by the gentiles until the times of the gentiles are filled.
21.25: “And there shall be signs in the sun, and moon, and stars, and on the earth anxiety of nations, in bewilderment at the roaring of the sea, and agitation,
21.26: men fainting from fear and the expectation of what is coming on the earth, for the powers of the shamayim shall be shaken.
21.27: “And then they shall see the Bĕn of Aḏam coming in a cloud with power and much esteem.
21.28: “And when these begin to take place, look up and lift up your heads, because your redemption draws near.”
21.29: And He spoke a parable to them, “Look at the fig tree, and all the trees.
21.30: “When they have already budded, observing it, you shall know for yourselves that summer is now near.
21.31: “So you also, when you see these take place, know that the Malḵuth of Elohim is near.
21.32: “Truly, I say to you, this generation shall by no means pass away till all shall have taken place.
21.33: “The shamayim and the earth shall pass away, but My Words shall by no means pass away.
21.34: “And take heed to yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down by gluttony, and drunkenness, and worries of this life, and that day come on you suddenly.
21.35: “For it shall come as a snare on all those dwelling on the face of all the earth.
21.36: “Watch then at all times, and pray that you be counted worthy to escape all this about to take place, and to stand before the Bĕn of Aḏam.”
21.37: And He was teaching in the Miqdash by day, but at night He went out and stayed on the mountain of Olives,
21.38: and early in the morning all the people came to Him in the Miqdash to hear Him.

22.1: And the Festival of Matstsoth drew near, which is called Pesaḥ.
22.2: And the chief kohenim and the scribes were seeking how to kill Him, for they feared the people.
22.3: And Satan entered into Yahuḏah, who was called of Qeriyoth, who was numbered among the twelve.
22.4: And he went and spoke with the chief kohenim and captains, how he might deliver Him up to them.
22.5: And they were glad, and agreed to give him silver.
22.6: And he promised, and was seeking an occasion to deliver Him up to them, away from the crowd.
22.7: And the Day of Matstsoth came when the Pesaḥ had to be slaughtered.
22.8: And He sent Kĕpha and Yoḥanan, saying, “Go and prepare the Pesaḥ for us to eat.”
22.9: And they said to Him, “Where do You want us to prepare?”
22.10: And He said to them, “See, as you enter into the city, a man shall meet you carrying a jar of water. Follow him into the house he enters.
22.11: “And you shall say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you, “Where is the guest room where I might eat the Pesaḥ with My talmidim?” ’
22.12: “And he shall show you a large, furnished upper room. Prepare it there.”
22.13: And going they found it as He had said to them, and they prepared the Pesaḥ.
22.14: And when the hour had come, He sat down, and the twelve emissaries with Him.
22.15: And He said to them, “With desire I have desired to eat this Pesaḥ with you before My suffering,
22.16: for I say to you, I shall certainly not eat of it again until it is filled in the Malḵuth of Elohim.”
22.17: And taking the cup, giving thanks, He said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves,
22.18: for I say to you, I shall certainly not drink of the fruit of the vine until the Malḵuth of Elohim comes.”
22.19: And taking bread, giving thanks, He broke it and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body which is given for you, do this in remembrance of Me.”
22.20: Likewise the cup also, after supper, saying, “This cup is the Renewed Covenant in My blood which is shed for you.
22.21: “But see, the hand of him delivering Me up is with Me on the table.
22.22: “For indeed the Bĕn of Aḏam goes as it has been decreed, but woe to that man by whom He is delivered up!”
22.23: And they began to ask among themselves, which of them it could be who was about to do this.
22.24: And there also took place a dispute among them, as to which of them seemed to be greater.
22.25: And He said to them, “The melaḵim of the gentiles rule over them, and those who control them are called ‘workers of good.’
22.26: “But not so with you, but let him who is greatest among you be as the youngest, and the leader as one who serves.
22.27: “For who is greater, the one who sits at the table, or the one who serves? Is it not the one who sits at the table? But I am in your midst as the One who serves.
22.28: “But you are those who have remained with Me in My trials.
22.29: “And I covenant for you, as My Father covenanted for Me, a Malḵuth,
22.30: to eat and drink at My table, in My Malḵuth, and to sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yisra’ĕl.”
22.31: And the Aḏon said, “Shim’on, Shim’on! See, Satan has asked for you to sift as wheat.
22.32: “But I have prayed for you, that your belief should not fail. And when you have turned, strengthen your brothers.”
22.33: And he said to Him, “Aḏonai, I am prepared to go with You, both to prison and to death.”
22.34: And He said, “I say to you, Kĕpha, the cock shall not crow at all today until you have denied three times that you know Me.”
22.35: And He said to them, “When I sent you without purse and bag and sandals, did you lack any?” And they said, “None at all.”
22.36: And He said to them, “But now, let him who has a purse take it, likewise also a bag. And let him who has no sword sell his garment and buy one.
